The page names no territory, so the region is the Maurya heartland of the maurya-empire dossier. ledger.note: 73 BCE: the minister Vasudeva Kanva seizes the throne. 'The Kanva dynasty was established by Vasudeva Kanva in 73 BCE'; 'Vasudeva was initially a minister of the Shunga Emperor Devabhuti,' who assassinated him and usurped the throne. The Shunga page: 'The Kanva dynasty succeeded the Shungas around 73 BCE'. Odisha removed (repair fx-28): the Shunga page never names Odisha or Kalinga land as held; 'After the decline of the Mauryan Empire, the region came under the control of the Mahameghavahana family' (Kalinga page) and the Mahameghavahana page has them in Kalinga ('conquered Kalinga and Kosala' in the first century B.C.), so the Cliopatria outline's northern Odisha (372 cells) is the mahameghavahana-dynasty core, not Shunga land.

wars.name: Shunga-Indo-Greek wars
wars.outcome: 'Pushyamitra successfully completed the Ashvamedha Yagna' after a battle on the Sindhu river in which Vasumitra defeated Greek cavalry; the Indo-Greeks 'either led by Demetrius I or Menander I' invaded and Menander 'is credited with either joining or leading a campaign to Pataliputra'. The two powers 'seem to have reconciled and exchanged diplomatic missions around 110 BCE'.
wars.note: The page dates none of the battles; the years bound Pushyamitra's accession and the reconciliation. No land is said to have changed hands, so no zone.

wars.name: Kharavela's campaigns against Magadha
wars.outcome: In his year 8 Kharavela's army 'laid siege to the city of Rajagriha' and in year 12 he 'subdues the king of Magadha'; the page does not name the Shunga and scholars disagree on the king's identity (Bahasatimita of Kaushambi and Magadha is one suggestion).
wars.note: The years are the Cliopatria Mahameghavahana row; the page gives Kharavela only to the '2nd or 1st century BC'. No land is said to have been held.

certainty.note: No frontier is dated or surveyed; the pages name capitals, viceroyalties and inscription findspots only. The Mathura and Punjab edges are the least certain.

notes:
Cliopatria row Shunga Empire -170..-67, 5 shapes. Five pages opened (budget 5). The Shunga page gives no area figure, so no ratio could be computed.

Departures from Cliopatria:
1. Start -184 (page: 'established in 184 BCE'; coup 185 BCE) instead of -170. The Maurya Empire shape of -188 is the stand-in for the first 14 years; the maurya-empire dossier ends in -185.
2. The -170..-165 shape (425,056 km2) is replaced by the -164 shape: it excludes Vidisha, which the page makes a court seat, and no page records a loss. The Cliopatria Mahameghavahana row of the same years (1,655,395 km2) overlaps the whole realm and is probably Kharavela's claim, not land held.
3. End -73 (Kanva page) instead of -67.

Not settled: (a) Shunga and Kanva as one state. Under master-plan rule 2 a dynasty that takes the same land by usurpation (Vasudeva, minister of the last Shunga, same capital, identical Cliopatria cells) would be a rename inside one dossier; I wrote the two separately because the brief lists both slugs, and note it for the orchestrator. (b) The Shunga remnant at Vidisha after -73, destroyed by the Andhras at an undated point (Satakarni II c. 50 BCE-0 or the 28 BCE end of the Kanvas). (c) How far Pushyamitra's writ ran west (Sialkot, Jalandhar, Mathura: the page's 'never ... under the direct control' for Mathura). (d) The 'Principality of Pataliputra' is named in the Kanva infobox but not explained. Rulers omitted: only Pushyamitra (187-151 BCE, 36 years) is dated on the page.
